THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
Challenging judgment and award dated 07.09.2016 passed by III Addl.
Senior Civil Judge at Kalaburagi (for short 'tribunal') in MVC no.863/2013, this appeal is filed.
2. Shri.

Shantanu Pradeep, learned counsel appearing for Sri Ganesh Naik and Sri A.S. Rawoor,
learned counsel for appellants submitted that appeal was by claimants for enhancement of compensation on account of death of minor aged 15 years.

It was submitted that on NC:
2023:KHC-K:7371 consideration, tribunal awarded inadequate compensation of Rs.3,98,000/-
including Rs.32,857/- towards medical expenses.
It was submitted that said award would be contrary to decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Kishan Gopal and another vs. Lala and others1.

entities.text: Kishan Gopal and another vs. Lala and others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was also submitted that application of multiplier corresponding to age of younger parent would also be erroneous and sought enhancement.

sentences.text: 2 3. On other hand, Shri.Manjunath Mallayya Shetty, learned counsel for respondent no.2-insurer submitted that compensation awarded by tribunal was just and proper and no enhancement was called for considering fact that deceased was minor.

4. Heard learned counsel, perused impugned judgment and award.
5.

From above submission and since only claimants were in appeal for enhancement of 2014 (1) SCC 244 NC: 2023:KHC-K:7371 compensation, finding of tribunal regarding death of minor girl aged about 15 years in accident that occurred on 11.05.2013 is not in dispute.
Issuance of insurance policy and its coverage as on date of accident are also not in dispute.
Claimants are parents.
As per ratio in case of Kishan Gopal (supra), notional annual income of minor has to be considered at Rs.30,000/-.

Though in said judgment multiplier applied was corresponding to age of younger parent, in view of Constitution Bench decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and others2, multiplier corresponding to age of deceased/victim has to be applied.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and others2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering multiplier corresponding to age of deceased as per said decision would be '18'.

Hence, compensation towards 'loss of dependency' would be Rs.5,40,000/- (Rs.30,000 x 18).
(2017) 16 SCC 680 NC: 2023:KHC-K:7371 6.
To said amount, Rs.32,857/- being amount spent towards medical expenses prior to death has to be added.
7. Thus, claimants are entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,72,857/-.
Tribunal has awarded total compensation of Rs.3,98,000/-.
Thereby, there is enhancement of Rs.1,74,857/-.

Hence, following:
ORDER i.
Appeal is allowed in part.
ii. Claimants are entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.1,74,857/ with interest at 6% p.a. from date of claim petition till deposit.
iii. Respondent no.2-insurer to deposit said amount within six weeks from date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
iv. Apportionment would be as per award of tribunal.

On deposit, sum of Rs.1,00,000/- is ordered to be released in favour of claimants and entire remaining amount with interest is ordered to be kept in Fixed Deposit in their names in any Nationalised Bank for a period of three years with liberty to withdraw interest periodically.
